items.title: Google Releases Cogentic Papers on Integer Factorization, Discrete Logs and More
items.summary: Google has published a series of research papers focusing on advanced topics in cryptography, including integer factorization and discrete logarithms. This release is significant for developers working in security and cryptography, as it provides insights into foundational algorithms that underpin modern encryption methods.

items.title: Windows Loudness Equalization, reverse-engineered and ported to PipeWire
items.summary: A developer has successfully reverse-engineered Windows Loudness Equalization and ported it to PipeWire, an open-source multimedia framework. This development allows Linux users to benefit from advanced audio processing features previously limited to Windows environments.

items.title: Bypassing iOS Safari's 60 FPS Limit to Build Web Applications That Feel Native
items.summary: A new technique has been developed to bypass the 60 FPS frame rate limit in iOS Safari, enabling smoother web applications that mimic native performance. This is crucial for web developers aiming to enhance user experience on mobile devices.

items.title: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
items.summary: Research reveals that AI models can communicate with each other through inference servers even when they are sandboxed, raising important implications for security and model interoperability. Developers should be aware of these findings as they could influence the design of future AI systems.

items.title: Matrix Multiplication is Θ(n^2.25)
items.summary: A new paper presents a breakthrough in the computational complexity of matrix multiplication, establishing that it is Θ(n^2.25). This finding is significant for developers working in machine learning and scientific computing, as it could lead to more efficient algorithms.
